name: shader
description: The OPTIONAL shader runtime of the effects layer (ADR 0022, ADR 0025): the gradient — one PARAMETRIC moving ground written for this library — and halo (light travelling round a surface that works or listens). fx("gradient") takes its look from a keyword token, --ui-fx-gradient-look: wash (a calm field), sweep (two big forms lit across their bodies), fold (light panes with lit rims), rise (a horizon with a crisp rim) or dawn (a soft horizon, light rising from below the frame); shared knobs tune any look — --ui-fx-gradient-angle, -sharpness, -scale, -chroma, -intensity, the quiet zone (-quiet, -quiet-x, -quiet-y) and -dissolve — and four knobs follow the look at auto (GRADIENT_PRESETS: angle, intensity, the quiet zone's size and height); knobs inherit, so a wrapper or brand scope can set them, the colours fall back to the scope's --ui-bg-base and --ui-bg-accent, numbers are read with their CSS unit and clamped to the range the GLSL is written for. Its palette is two tokens (--ui-fx-gradient-base, --ui-fx-gradient-light) with every other tone derived in OKLab; chroma falls with lightness and darker tones turn their hue away from yellow-green, so a pale-yellow brand's shadows go amber, not olive. Every pixel ends in a static one-step triangular dither, so slow ramps never band; a ground renders at full resolution and at most 30fps. startShaders() — server-safe, reference-counted, returns its stop function — finds every .fx-gradient / .fx-halo root, mounts one canvas in the part the effect paints and draws it from tokens read where that part sits, through ONE shared WebGL2 context. A shader is admitted only if it paints pixels it owns, takes every input from a token, keeps the component as its floor and keeps the ink on its part legible — the gradient by a QUIET ZONE of its exact base around the copy, so the ink keeps its audited contrast while the light elsewhere is free; check:fx enforces the first two on the sources, the browser test the last two on drawn pixels under the real text, for every look, scheme and the pale-yellow stress brand. Forced colours draw nothing (the floor). The gradient's floor is a still, faint CSS gradient of the same light. The aurora effect was retired 2026-11-22. The canvas draws the part's own rounded shape (iOS Safari drops a CSS clip on an animating canvas), covers the border box, and follows the component's own state transitions through a registered property (--ui-fx-halo-strength). State is published on the root as data-fx-gradient / data-fx-halo (live, still, floor, lost, unsupported); reduced motion draws one chosen still frame and the loop sleeps when nothing moves. configureShaders() and sampleShader() (pixels and the resolved uniform values) exist for stories and contrast tests.
